family.description: Members of this family catalyse the reduction of the 5,6-double bond of a uridine residue on tRNA. Dihydrouridine modification of tRNA is widely observed in prokaryotes and eukaryotes, and also in some archae. Most dihydrouridines are found in the D loop of t-RNAs. The role of dihydrouridine in tRNA is currently unknown, but may increase conformational flexibility of the tRNA. It is likely that different family members have different substrate specificities, which may overlap. Dus 1 ([swissprot:Q9HGN6]) from Saccharomyces cerevisiae acts on pre-tRNA-Phe, while Dus 2 ([swissprot:P53720]) acts on pre-tRNA-Tyr and pre-tRNA-Leu. Dus 1 is active as a single subunit, requiring NADPH or NADH, and is stimulated by the presence of FAD [[cite:PUB00014304]]. Some family members may be targeted to the mitochondria and even have a role in mitochondria [[cite:PUB00014304]].
family.name: Dihydrouridine synthase (Dus)

history.description: Read Rider 2009 Methods, Results and Discussion and visually inspected Figures 2-5 and 8. Verified P53720/PF01207 reference mapping, retained five direct observed effects in separate NADPH, synthetic-RNA, knockout-derived-RNA and bacterial-RNA contexts, and recorded source concentration/template/primer discrepancies. Excluded mutant-specific causal edges because printed primers disagree at H120/Q120 and the oxidative comparison uses different temperatures. Added a later DusA abstract lead, minimal evidence and open follow-up; IN_PROGRESS, no publication.

causal_graphs.context: Mix 15 uM oxidized enzyme with anaerobic NADPH concentration series at 4 C in 100 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl2 and 10% glycerol. Stopped-flow absorbance at 450 nm measures flavin reduction. DTT is removed immediately before assays.

evidence.explanation: Figure 2 was visually inspected with the reductive-half-reaction Results and anaerobic kinetics Methods; small secondary phases remain qualified.
Current exact reference/domain mapping supports member scope without independently reconstructing the historical expression clone.

edges.mechanism: NADPH addition produces a concentration-dependent major decrease in oxidized-flavin absorbance. The edge records the experimentally observed redox conversion, not a complete catalytic cycle or inferred product-release trajectory.
edges.subject: add-nadph-to-oxidized-dus2

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P53720/DUS2_YEAST is SMM1/DUS2/YNR015W, 384 aa, sequence version 1, with PF01207 at 32-352. UniProt and InterPro sequences agree. The study uses the supplied pEfx-4b yeast DUS2 plasmid and BL21(DE3) expression, cobalt-affinity and DEAE purification. Exact historical tag junctions and clone sequence remain unverified.
causal_graphs.limitations: Minor slower spectral phases may reflect damaged protein. The observed reduction does not independently establish the proposed NADP dissociation rate or every hydride-transfer microstep. FMN in this preparation is not a claim that all family members have identical cofactor or substrate behavior.

nodes.label: Mix NADPH with anaerobic oxidized WT Dus2
Reduced enzyme-bound flavin measured by A450 loss

causal_graphs.scope: Recombinant WT Saccharomyces cerevisiae Dus2 in Rider 2009 Figure 2 and reductive-half-reaction Results. This is an anaerobic purified-protein assay, not cellular RNA modification.
causal_graphs.title: NADPH reduces the flavin of purified yeast Dus2

causal_graphs.context: Dithionite-prereduced enzyme reacts anaerobically at 25 C in the pH-7.5 HEPES/NaCl/MgCl2/glycerol buffer. Results give 60 uM enzyme and 700 uM RNA, whereas the caption gives 35 uM enzyme. Flavin reoxidation is followed over hours; a separate alkaline-ring-opening A550 colorimetric assay measures dihydrouridine against a standard curve.

evidence.explanation: Figure 3 spectra were visually inspected; adjacent product-analysis Results and colorimetric Methods establish the separate chemical endpoint and its limitations.

edges.mechanism: Reaction of the reduced enzyme with the reported RNA preparation yields dihydrouridine alongside flavin oxidation. The evidence supports net product formation, not the exact order of binding, proton transfer and release.
edges.subject: prereduced-dus2-synthetic-trna

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Intact yeast Dus2 maps to P53720 and PF01207 32-352. The published pre/intronless template strings differ by a promoter-containing prefix rather than an evident intron, so the exact assayed RNA sequence is not reconstructed from those strings.
causal_graphs.limitations: The enzyme concentration and 450/457-nm reporting differ between caption and Results. Product colorimetry supports dihydrouridine formation but is not site-resolved sequencing or mass spectrometry. Exact RNA sequence, matched no-enzyme raw data and stoichiometry were not independently verified; no precise kinetic constant or C117 proton-transfer edge is adopted.

nodes.label: React prereduced WT Dus2 with reported synthetic pre-tRNA-Leu

causal_graphs.scope: WT yeast Dus2 acting on the reported synthetic pre-tRNA-Leu preparation in Figure 3 and oxidative-half-reaction Results. No nucleotide position is independently assigned by this endpoint.
causal_graphs.title: Prereduced Dus2 forms dihydrouridine in a synthetic tRNA preparation

causal_graphs.context: Anaerobic 20 uM Dus2 is reduced with dithionite and mixed with RNA at 4 C in 100 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl2 and 10% glycerol. A450 increases in stopped-flow experiments. The caption gives RNA up to 800 uM; the plotted concentration axis says mM.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 4 and read native-RNA purification and kinetics Methods; Figure 5's different mutant conditions constrain, rather than extend, this edge.

edges.mechanism: The purified knockout-derived RNA preparation oxidizes the prereduced flavin in the WT enzyme. Separate preparation and temperature effects are not collapsed into an isolated modification-specific causal claim.
edges.subject: add-knockout-derived-trna-to-dus2

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The protein is the same P53720-mapped WT yeast Dus2 preparation, PF01207 32-352. The RNA source is specified by YNR015w deletion, but its exact strain identifier, full modification inventory and oligonucleotide sequence were not independently established.
causal_graphs.limitations: This edge records flavin oxidation, not an independently localized D20 product. The substrate-preparation comparison to synthetic RNA and the C117A comparison use different temperatures. Neither an exact fold improvement nor a specific required prior modification is asserted. The caption/image concentration discrepancy remains open.

nodes.label: Add knockout-derived tRNA-Leu to prereduced WT Dus2
Reoxidized enzyme-bound flavin measured by A450 increase

causal_graphs.scope: WT yeast Dus2 with affinity-purified tRNA-Leu from a YNR015w knockout in Figure 4. The RNA is partially matured, not an unmodified in-vitro transcript.
causal_graphs.title: Knockout-derived tRNA-Leu reoxidizes reduced WT Dus2

causal_graphs.context: Treat 90 uM bulk E. coli tRNA with 40 uM Dus2 aerobically for 18 h and assay dihydrouridine content. General kinetics default to 4 C, but the endpoint paragraph does not explicitly restate temperature. Do not borrow the anaerobic stopped-flow conditions as an exact endpoint recipe.

evidence.explanation: Reverse-reaction Results and colorimetric Methods were inspected; this reported endpoint is separate from the visually inspected Figure 8 spectral trace.

edges.mechanism: The aerobic enzyme treatment reduces the measured dihydrouridine content of the RNA mixture, supporting reverse biochemical activity in this context. It does not establish which yeast RNA sites would undergo a reverse reaction in cells.
edges.subject: aerobic-dus2-treatment-ecoli-trna

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The enzyme maps to P53720 with PF01207 32-352; the bacterial RNA mixture is a separate substrate whose strain and individual tRNA composition are not resolved. It is not a pure yeast physiological system.
causal_graphs.limitations: The measured content decreases but is not eliminated. The assay does not identify each affected tRNA or nucleotide, measure cellular reverse flux, or independently characterize every oxidation product. Oxygen-supported endpoint turnover is distinct from the short anaerobic spectral assay.

nodes.label: Treat bulk E. coli tRNA with yeast Dus2 aerobically for 18 h
Colorimetric dihydrouridine content of the bulk bacterial tRNA

causal_graphs.scope: Recombinant yeast Dus2 with bulk E. coli tRNA in the 18-h reverse-reaction experiment. This is a mixed-species in-vitro endpoint.
causal_graphs.title: Aerobic yeast Dus2 treatment lowers dihydrouridine in bulk bacterial tRNA

causal_graphs.context: Mix anaerobic enzyme and RNA at 4 C in 100 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl2 and 10% glycerol. Dus2 is 20 uM after mixing; stopped-flow A450 decrease is fitted with two phases.

evidence.explanation: Figure 8 was visually inspected with its caption and reverse-reaction Results; the paper explicitly warns against assigning mixture kinetics to a pure yeast system.

edges.mechanism: The bacterial RNA mixture reduces the enzyme-bound flavin under anaerobic conditions. Together with the separately measured aerobic content loss this supports biochemical reversibility, but the assays are not represented as one observed molecular trajectory.
edges.subject: add-bulk-ecoli-trna-to-oxidized-dus2

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P53720 yeast Dus2 contains PF01207 32-352; the bacterial tRNA is a heterogeneous substrate pool. The shared enzyme identity does not make these mixed-species half-reactions a directly tracked native cycle.
causal_graphs.limitations: RNA composition and individual reaction sites are unresolved. Fitted mixture rate constants are not intrinsic constants for a single yeast tRNA. The smaller spectral phase and potential damaged enzyme are not extra molecular intermediates.

nodes.label: Mix bulk E. coli tRNA with anaerobic oxidized yeast Dus2
Reduced enzyme-bound flavin measured by A450 loss

causal_graphs.scope: Oxidized WT yeast Dus2 with bulk E. coli tRNA in Rider 2009 Figure 8, distinct from the aerobic 18-h content assay.
causal_graphs.title: Bulk bacterial tRNA reduces the flavin of yeast Dus2 anaerobically
